deed: צוותי סיוע ישראליים סייעו בשיקום מיאנמר לאחר ציקלון קטלני
title: Israeli aid teams went to Myanmar after Cyclone Nargis, with doctors, nurses and water specialists

trailer.text: IsraAID is an Israeli aid organization whose executive members represent 15 non-governmental organizations in Israel.
In early May 2008 Cyclone Nargis struck Myanmar, and according to JTA more than a million people were left without homes, without food and without safe drinking water.
IsraAID decided to send a small team of doctors, nurses and water specialists, volunteers from the Israeli organizations F.I.R.S.T and Israeli Flying Aid.
The team arrived in the area on May 8, to treat the sick and to help determine which water was safe to drink.

According to a report published on the day the delegations departed, the Foreign Ministry sent teams, and Israel also sent supplies, including plastic sheeting, food, household appliances and water filters.

paragraphs.text: Nargis was a Category 4 cyclone on the Saffir-Simpson scale.
It struck Myanmar in early May 2008.
According to ISRAEL21c, some experts believe its impact could be worse than that of the 2004 tsunami if aid is not flown in immediately.
According to the UN, more than a million people needed shelter and life-saving aid.
According to the UN, 5,000 km² of the delta region were flooded.
According to ISRAEL21c, the survivors were left homeless, short of food and safe drinking water.
The military junta declared three days of mourning in memory of the victims.
How many people were killed? The sources give very different numbers.
Shahar Zahavi, director of IsraAID, said the organization decided to look for a way to help after they saw on TV what was happening in Burma.
IsraAID decided to send a small team of doctors, nurses and water specialists, to provide immediate relief.
According to ISRAEL21c, IsraAID also sent relief after the 2004 tsunami and after Hurricane Katrina.
According to ISRAEL21c, donations to fund the Israeli relief came from organizations and individuals around the world.
A small Jewish community existed in Burma from the 19th century.
At its peak it numbered 1,200 people.
The volunteers were selected from two Israeli non-governmental organizations: F.I.R.S.T and Israeli Flying Aid.
The team was headed by Dr. Ephraim Laor, described as Israel's leading rescue expert, who is in direct contact with the UN.
The team went out under the umbrella of IsraAID and in cooperation with the UN.
Zahavi said Myanmar would provide visas for the teams by Wednesday morning.
The team arrived in the area on May 8.
It was expected to stay three weeks.
The Israeli aid organization Latet was also about to send two people to survey the area and assess the urgent aid needs.
According to JTA, a Latet team arrived in Myanmar two days after the IsraAID team.
The Israeli doctors and nurses set out to treat the sick.
The water specialists set out to help assess which water was safest for immediate drinking.
The team was also charged with reporting back to Israel on the next stages of relief.
According to Arutz Sheva, Israel's search and rescue teams are expert in extracting survivors from rubble.
According to a report published on the day the delegations departed, the Foreign Ministry sent teams from the IDF search-and-rescue unit.
According to the same report, a team of 10 Israeli doctors and nurses was also sent.
Israel sent needed supplies: plastic sheeting, food, household appliances and water filters.
The Foreign Ministry also issued a travel warning for Israeli tourists in Myanmar, because of heavy damage to infrastructure.
A spokesman for the Myanmar Embassy in Tel Aviv expressed appreciation to the Israeli government and to the non-governmental organizations that helped.
Eran Weintraub, director of Latet, said he was filled with pride that on the eve of Israel's 60th Independence Day, Israelis have the power to offer help.
According to IsraAID, Nargis in 2008 was one of its three emergency responses in Myanmar, and was followed by a response to floods in 2015.
The EU envoy in Yangon said reconstruction would take much more than a year.
Myanmar's ruling junta placed obstacles before foreign aid missions.
Aid organization and UN staff had difficulty obtaining entry permits.
The military regime hinted that it would agree to accept supplies, but would not let in foreign aid teams.
According to ynet, the Myanmar authorities at first refused to accept international help.
A spokesman for the UN food programme complained that international medical personnel were not receiving visas, and that essential food was also being held up.
France's ambassador to the UN said the delays to the medical aid missions bordered on a crime against humanity.
Weintraub said that in the first days Myanmar's rulers did not let relief workers into the area, and changed course after realizing they needed help.
Zahavi said the Israeli team had encountered no problems with the Myanmar Embassy in Tel Aviv, and foresaw no problems ahead.

disagreements.question: How many people were killed in Cyclone Nargis?

versions.says: Myanmar's foreign minister confirmed 10,000 dead on May 5
According to Ynetnews, at least 22,500 dead
According to Walla!, local media reported 22,980 dead, 42,119 missing and 1,383 injured
According to Arutz Sheva and Ynetnews, about 23,000 dead
According to Arutz Sheva, aid organizations estimated more than 50,000 dead, and 41,000 missing
The government of Myanmar reported 78 thousand dead
According to HaMichlol, the official count stood at about 78,000 dead and about 56,000 missing
According to ISRAEL21c, some aid organizations estimated up to 100,000 dead
According to information received by the American embassy, and sources at the UN and the Red Cross, more than 100 thousand dead
According to Walla!, in a later report the number rose to 133 thousand
In the infobox of the Hamichlol entry, the death toll is estimated at 146,000.

The insurance company Harel announced that it would dispatch a search-and-rescue mission to locate Amit Efrati, 26, from Tzur Hadassah, one of two Israelis missing in the area, and we have no information on whether he was found.
